verdict.rationale: Better Auth is an npm-installed library that you instantiate in your own app. Its docs state it requires a database to store user data and can be configured for SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL and more, and it is described as a self-hosted framework. Community users independently confirm that all auth data lives in their own DB with no DB-provider lock-in. Missing for 10: a dedicated first-party guide on deployment topology or data residency (e.g. private/isolated instance hardening).

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can control where the auth system and its user data run — self-managed deployment, private instance, or my own database

citations.quote: Better Auth requires a database to store user data. You can easily configure Better Auth to use SQLite, PostgreSQL, or MySQL, and more!
Better Auth is a self-hosted framework
You get all of your auth data in your own db in 1 cli command. You are not tied to any db provider.
It just works and I own all the data.
